title: You Are Mine
why: Comfort lane, same as Be Still / Fret Not. The hook is verse 2 almost verbatim; 43:25 is the half-tempo spoken bridge, so the arc ends big.

sections.label: Hook
lines: Fear not, I formed you, I called you by name,
Through the water, through the fire, you come out the same.
You are mine, you are mine, that's what the Maker said,
Precious in his sight, so I'm lifting up my head.

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: He who created Jacob, who formed Israel, said
"Do not fear, I redeemed you" — put his name on my head.
Through the waters he's with me, the rivers won't drown,
Through the fire I don't burn, not a flame on me now.
I'm precious in his sight, I'm honored, I'm loved,
He paid out whole nations for the one he thought of.
From the east bring my children, from the west gather in,
North, give 'em up; south, don't hold 'em — bring 'em home again.

sections.label: Hook
lines: Fear not, I formed you, I called you by name,
Through the water, through the fire, you come out the same.
You are mine, you are mine, that's what the Maker said,
Precious in his sight, so I'm lifting up my head.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Bring the blind that got eyes, bring the deaf that got ears,
Let the nations stand up, let the witness appear.
Who called out the first things, who can say it in advance?
You're my witness, says Yahweh, this was never happenstance.
No god formed before me, ain't a god after me,
No savior but the one who cut the road through the sea.
I declared it, I saved you, no stranger in the room,
No hand delivers out of mine — who undoes what I do?

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: He made a way through the water, cut a path through the deep,
Horse and chariot and army went out like a wick in its sleep.
"Don't remember the former, don't you dwell on what's gone,
Behold, I'm doing a new thing — can't you see it come on?"
Rivers in the desert, and a way where there's none,
Streams in the wilderness for the people he formed.
Didn't bring him my lambs, didn't burn him my spice,
Only brought him my sin, made him carry the weight —
And still:

sections.label: Bridge - half tempo, spoken
lines: "For my own sake,
for my own sake,
I blot out your transgressions.
I will not remember your sins.
Put me in remembrance. Plead your case."

sections.label: Hook - final, big
lines: Fear not, I formed you, I called you by name,
Through the water, through the fire, you come out the same.
You are mine, you are mine, that's what the Maker said,
Precious in his sight, so I'm lifting up my head.
Behold, he's doing a new thing — can't you see it break through?
Rivers in the desert, and the desert was you.

title: Here Am I
why: Throne -> 'woe, I am undone' -> the coal -> 'send me'. Only 8 couplets, so it rides on hook repetition: 'Holy, holy, holy' is the chant.

sections.label: Hook
lines: Holy, holy, holy — Yahweh of Armies, King,
Whole earth full of glory and the door posts ring.
I said, "Woe, I'm undone" — then the coal touched my mouth,
Here am I, send me. Here am I, send me out.

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: The year the king died, I saw the Lord enthroned,
High and lifted up, and his train filled the holy home.
Six-winged seraphs calling out across the hall,
"Holy, holy, holy" — and the whole earth's full.
The caller's voice hit the thresholds, foundations quaked,
And the house filled up with smoke, filling all of the space.
I'm standing in the light with nowhere left to hide,
A man of unclean lips in the room where the King resides.

sections.label: Hook
lines: Holy, holy, holy — Yahweh of Armies, King,
Whole earth full of glory and the door posts ring.
I said, "Woe, I'm undone" — then the coal touched my mouth,
Here am I, send me. Here am I, send me out.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: "Woe is me, I'm undone" — that's the cry that came out,
Unclean lips, and I live where the lips are unclean now.
My eyes have seen the King, Yahweh of Armies, and I
Should have been ash on the floor, but I'm somehow alive.
Then a seraph took a live coal from the altar in flight,
Touched it to my mouth — didn't soothe me, it ignited.
"Your iniquity is taken, and your sin is atoned,"
And the mouth that said "unclean" is the mouth he now owns.

sections.label: Bridge - half tempo, spoken
lines: Then the voice of the Lord:
"Whom shall I send?
And who will go for us?"
And I said — before I knew what it would cost —
"Here am I. Send me."

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: He said, "Go and tell this people: hear, but never understand,
See, but don't perceive it" — that's the word he put in my hand.
"Make the heart fat, the ears heavy, shut the eyes tight,
Lest they turn and I heal them" — that's a heavy thing to write.
I said, "Lord, how long?" He said, "Till the cities lie waste,
Till the houses have no people and the land is a bare place.
Till a tenth is consumed, and consumed once again —"
But the stump that's left standing is the holy seed. Amen.

sections.label: Hook - final, big
lines: Holy, holy, holy — Yahweh of Armies, King,
Whole earth full of glory and the door posts ring.
I said, "Woe, I'm undone" — then the coal touched my mouth,
Here am I, send me. Here am I, send me out.
The stump is still standing, there's a seed in the ground,
Here am I, send me. Here am I, send me out.

title: No Money No Price
why: Most accessible. 'Come, thirsty ones -- no money, no price' is already a hook.

sections.label: Hook
lines: Come, all you thirsty, come down to the water and buy,
Wine and milk and bread — no money, no price.
Why you spending what you got on what was never bread?
Come and eat what is good, let your soul be fed.

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: Ho, everyone thirsty, come down to the stream,
No coin in your pocket, but the table's still free.
Buy the wine, buy the milk, and the cost of it is nil,
Why you labor for a wage that was never gonna fill?
Listen close to me, eat good, let your soul take delight,
Turn your ear, come to God, and your soul comes alive.
He says, "I'll cut a pact with you that doesn't run out,
The sure mercies of David — that's what this is about."

sections.label: Hook
lines: Come, all you thirsty, come down to the water and buy,
Wine and milk and bread — no money, no price.
Why you spending what you got on what was never bread?
Come and eat what is good, let your soul be fed.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: He gave him as a witness to the peoples, a guide,
A leader and commander to the nations worldwide.
Now a nation that never knew you comes running at the sound,
'Cause Yahweh, the Holy One, has glorified you now.
So seek him while he's found, call on him while he's near,
Let the wicked leave his way and his thoughts — come here.
He pardons, and he pardons like the debt was never owed,
That's the only kind of math that his mercy has known.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: "My thoughts are not your thoughts, and my ways are not yours,"
As high as the heavens over earth, that's how far.
Like the rain and like the snow coming down from the sky,
They don't go back up till the ground is satisfied —
Till it waters and it buds and it gives seed and bread,
So the word out of his mouth does the thing that he said.
It will not come back empty, it will finish what it starts,
And you'll go out with joy and the peace will lead you out.

sections.label: Hook - final, big
lines: Come, all you thirsty, come down to the water and buy,
Wine and milk and bread — no money, no price.
Why you spending what you got on what was never bread?
Come and eat what is good, let your soul be fed.
The mountains and the hills break out into song,
And the trees of the field clap their hands all along.
Where the thorn was, a cypress; where the brier, a myrtle tree,
Standing as a sign to his name eternally.

title: Rise Like Eagles
why: The big anthem. Dense list material trimmed -- see the sheet's footer.
note: Trimmed from the rhyme text: Lebanon's beasts as burnt offerings, and the cast-idol/gold-overlay couplet. Both are list material that raps badly and neither carries the chapter's argument the way the "who measured" lines do.

sections.label: Hook
lines: They that wait on the Lord will renew their strength,
Rise up like eagles on a wind off the edge.
Run and not be weary, walk and not faint,
The grass is gonna wither but his word's gonna stay.

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: Comfort, comfort my people — that's the word from the throne,
Tell Jerusalem her warfare's over, her sin is atoned.
She's received of his hand double for all that she's done,
And a voice in the wilderness is saying, "Prepare for the One."
Make it level, make it straight, raise the valley from the low,
Bring the mountain and the hill down where the highway's gonna go.
Then the glory of the Lord is gonna show for every eye,
'Cause the mouth of Yahweh spoke it — that's the only reason why.

sections.label: Hook
lines: They that wait on the Lord will renew their strength,
Rise up like eagles on a wind off the edge.
Run and not be weary, walk and not faint,
The grass is gonna wither but his word's gonna stay.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: All flesh is grass and the glory is a flower in the field,
The grass withers, the flower fades, and that's the whole deal.
But the word of our God is still standing when it's bare,
So go up on the mountain, lift your voice, cast off fear.
Say it loud to the cities of Judah: "Behold your God!"
He is coming with a ruling arm and the wage that he brought.
But the same arm that rules is the arm that gathers lambs,
Holds them up against his chest, leads the mothers by hand.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: Who measured out the waters in the hollow of a hand?
Who spanned the sky, who weighed the mountains, who set the scale to stand?
Nobody counseled him, nobody taught him the way,
And the nations are a drop in the bucket on that scale.
He sits above the circle of the earth, and from that height
We look like grasshoppers — he spread the sky out like a tent at night.
He brings the princes down to nothing, blows the judges away,
Like a withered piece of stubble, and there's no trace where they lay.

sections.label: Bridge - half tempo, spoken
lines: "Lift up your eyes. Who created these?
He brings out their host by number.
He calls them every one by name.
Not one of them is missing."
So why do you say it, Jacob —
"My way is hidden from the Lord,
and the justice due me is passed over by my God"?

sections.label: Hook - final, big
lines: Have you not known? Have you not heard it before?
The everlasting God, the Creator, don't get worn.
He don't faint, he don't tire, and his wisdom has no end,
He gives power to the fainting, and the weak, he gives strength.
They that wait on the Lord will renew their strength,
Rise up like eagles on a wind off the edge.
Run and not be weary, walk and not faint,
The grass is gonna wither but his word's gonna stay.

title: Where You Go
why: Best hook in the whole corpus and it was already written: 'where you go, I'll go... your God, my God.' Ends dark on 'call me Mara', which is the spoken bridge, so the final hook has to lift against it.

sections.label: Hook
lines: Where you go, I'll go; where you stay, I'll stay,
Your people are my people, and your God is my God.
Where you die, I'll die, and they'll lay me where you lay,
Let the Lord do worse to me if I turn from this road.

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: Famine came to Bethlehem and the house of bread went dry,
So Elimelech took Naomi and his two sons to survive.
Moab was a season, not a country, not a home,
Then Elimelech died and left Naomi on her own.
The sons took Moabite wives, Orpah and Ruth by name,
Ten years in a borrowed field, and then the second wave came.
Both sons died — no husband, and no children, and no claim,
Just three widows in a field and a God she wants to blame.

sections.label: Hook
lines: Where you go, I'll go; where you stay, I'll stay,
Your people are my people, and your God is my God.
Where you die, I'll die, and they'll lay me where you lay,
Let the Lord do worse to me if I turn from this road.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Then she heard that Yahweh gave his people bread again,
So she set out on the Judah road with both her daughters then.
"Go home," she told them. "May Yahweh deal kind with you,
May he give you rest in a husband's house — there's nothing here for you."
They wept and said, "No, we'll go back with you instead,"
She said, "Are there sons left in my womb? Is there a husband in my bed?
Yahweh's hand has gone out against me; I'm too bitter to be near" —
And Orpah kissed her, turned around, and disappeared.

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: But Ruth held on, and Ruth clung, and Ruth would not turn away,
Naomi saw the set of her face and had nothing left to say.
So the two of them walked into Bethlehem, and the whole town stirred,
"Is this Naomi?" — and you could hear the doubt in the word.

sections.label: Bridge - half tempo, spoken
lines: "Don't call me Naomi.
Call me Mara,
because the Almighty has dealt bitterly with me.
I went out full.
Yahweh has brought me home empty.
Why call me pleasant
when he has testified against me?"

sections.label: Hook - final, big
lines: Where you go, I'll go; where you stay, I'll stay,
Your people are my people, and your God is my God.
Where you die, I'll die, and they'll lay me where you lay,
Let the Lord do worse to me if I turn from this road.
She came home empty and she said it out loud,
But the barley harvest started the day she got to town.
Where you go, I'll go — and she went. And she stayed.
And the empty house of bread had bread again.

title: Salvation Belongs
why: First person from inside the fish. 7 couplets, the shortest sheet here, so like Isaiah 6 it carries on repetition. The turn ('I remembered Yahweh') is the bridge, placed before verse 2 so the song goes down, turns, then rises.

sections.label: Hook
lines: Salvation belongs to Yahweh — say it from the deep,
Say it with the water in your lungs and the weeds on your feet.
I went down to the bottom and the bottom wasn't the end,
He heard me from the belly. Salvation belongs to him.

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: Out of the belly of Sheol I called, and he heard me,
From the heart of the sea where the current had turned me.
You threw me in the deep — I'm not blaming the crew,
Every breaker, every billow passing over me was you.
I said, "I'm driven from your sight" — then I said the other thing:
"Yet I will look again toward your holy temple, King."
The waters closed in on my soul, the deep was all around,
Weeds were wrapped around my head and the earth barred me down.

sections.label: Hook
lines: Salvation belongs to Yahweh — say it from the deep,
Say it with the water in your lungs and the weeds on your feet.
I went down to the bottom and the bottom wasn't the end,
He heard me from the belly. Salvation belongs to him.

sections.label: Bridge - half tempo, spoken
lines: Down to the roots of the mountains.
The earth with her bars closed behind me.
And when my soul fainted within me —
I remembered Yahweh.
And my prayer came in to you,
into your holy temple.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: Then you brought my life up out of the pit where I lay,
And the man who ran from the word is the man who stayed to pray.
Everybody clinging to a lie that cannot hold
forsakes the only mercy that was ever his to own.
So I'll sacrifice with thanksgiving, I will pay what I vowed,
I'll say it in the dark the way I'd say it in the crowd.
Three days in the dark and I learned the whole of it:
He don't need the dry land to hear a man repent.

sections.label: Hook - final, big
lines: Salvation belongs to Yahweh — say it from the deep,
Say it with the water in your lungs and the weeds on your feet.
I went down to the bottom and the bottom wasn't the end,
He heard me from the belly. Salvation belongs to him.
Then Yahweh spoke one word and the fish obeyed the sound,
And it put me on the dry land, and I'm standing on the ground.

title: For Such A Time
why: 'Perhaps this time you came to reign' is the hook. Mordecai's speech is the spoken bridge, and 'if I perish, I perish' is the big finish.

sections.label: Hook
lines: Who knows but that you came to the kingdom for this,
For such a time as this, for such a time as this.
If I perish, I perish — but I'm walking in there,
Three days with no water, and I'm going on a prayer.

sections.label: Verse 1
lines: Mordecai heard the decree and he tore what he wore,
Put on sackcloth and ashes, went out crying in the road.
Every province where the writing of the king had been read,
There was fasting, there was weeping, there was sackcloth and dread.
Esther heard her man was mourning and it shook her,
Sent him clothes to change into — he would not take them from her.
So she called for Hathach: "Go find out the what and the why,"
Met him in the open square by the king's gate outside.

sections.label: Hook
lines: Who knows but that you came to the kingdom for this,
For such a time as this, for such a time as this.
If I perish, I perish — but I'm walking in there,
Three days with no water, and I'm going on a prayer.

sections.label: Verse 2
lines: He told him about Haman and the silver he weighed,
Handed him the decree: "Take it to her. Tell her plead."
She sent it back: "There's a law that everybody knows —
You don't walk in uncalled where the inner court goes.
One law. You die. Unless he holds the gold scepter out.
And he has not called for me in thirty days. That's the count."

sections.label: Bridge - half tempo, spoken
lines: And Mordecai sent back:
"Don't imagine you'll escape in the king's house
any more than the rest of the Jews.
If you stay silent now,
relief will come from somewhere else —
but you and your father's house will perish.
And who knows
whether you have come to the kingdom
for such a time as this?"

sections.label: Verse 3
lines: She said, "Go and gather every Jew in Susa, all of them,
Fast for me three days, three nights, no water and no bread.
Me and all my maidens, we will fast the same way,
Then I'll go in to the king against the law — and if I die, I die."
Mordecai went his way and he did everything she said,
Same man who was wailing with the ashes on his head.
The one who had been telling her is the one who obeyed,
And the queen who can't be summoned is the one who named the day.

sections.label: Hook - final, big
lines: Who knows but that you came to the kingdom for this,
For such a time as this, for such a time as this.
If I perish, I perish — but I'm walking in there,
Three days with no water, and I'm going on a prayer.
Not the scepter, not the law, not the thirty days of silence —
She put her whole house on a maybe and she walked in.
